title: Wedjat D011-D016 against all other Unicode Egyptian hieroglyphs: executed modern-glyph negative control
purpose: Test the D011-D016 Wedjat fraction glyphs against the full original Unicode Egyptian Hieroglyphs block so that visual regularities are not judged without a large unrelated-hieroglyph baseline.

test_A_geometric_halving_against_50000_r.hypothesis: If the physical rendered geometry itself encoded repeated halving, the ordered D011-D016 metrics should approximate lambda=0.5 and outperform random ordered six-glyph sets.
test_A_geometric_halving_against_50000_r.interpretation: All three fitted lambdas are near 1.1, not 0.5, and random hieroglyph sets are frequently as dyadic or better. The exact six-bit structure therefore resides in the assigned fraction values, not in progressive rendered glyph size.

test_B_shape_family_and_other_hieroglyph.descriptor: robust-z morphology vector using aspect, ink density, normalized perimeter, skeleton length, endpoints, junctions, components, holes, Hu moments and coarse projections
test_B_shape_family_and_other_hieroglyph.notable_false_positive_pressure: D016 has an especially close unrelated modern-glyph neighbor: its nearest-neighbor distance lies near the 6th percentile of the control nearest-neighbor distribution. Shape resemblance alone is therefore unsafe as a genealogy criterion.

test_C_morphological_complexity.interpretation: The modern complexity score happens to rank the six signs broadly in the same direction as Ritter's diagnosticity discussion, but this comparison was not preregistered, has n=6, and cannot make a modern font paleographic evidence.

test_D_other_fraction_hieroglyphs_and_no.ancient_text_control: UCL Lahun UC32159 is a Middle Kingdom 2:n unit-fraction table; UCL's worked description explicitly includes 1/3 and 1/15 in the 2:5 row.
test_D_other_fraction_hieroglyphs_and_no.interpretation: The 1/2..1/64 capacity-submultiple ladder is mathematically dyadic, but Egyptian fraction reckoning also used non-dyadic fractions. Any binary analogy must remain local to that dyadic sequence.

important_points: Ritter treats 1/16 and 1/32 as especially diagnostic hieratic forms, 1/2 as intermediate, and 1/4, 1/8 and 1/64 as less diagnostic.
Ritter reports that earlier third-millennium hieratic CSM signs increasingly diverge from the supposed Horus-eye counterparts.
Ritter identifies administration, mathematics and medical texts among the historical CSM source families, making cross-document and cross-domain testing appropriate.

highest_admissible_claim: The full-block modern-hieroglyph control rejects the idea that the rendered D011-D016 shapes themselves geometrically halve with their 1/2..1/64 values, and shows substantial false-positive pressure from unrelated glyph morphology. The exact dyadic/six-bit mathematics remains real for the assigned value sequence, but it is not a general property of Egyptian fractions and is not evidence of ancient binary or Python intent. The next decisive test must use SHA-256-sealed, dated ancient CSM sign occurrences with same-document non-target hieratic controls.

next_gate.required: Acquire exact institutional image/facsimile bytes for dated CSM occurrences, SHA-256 seal before scoring, localize signs by edition locator, and compare each target against same-document stroke/complexity-matched non-target hieratic signs.
next_gate.minimum: 60 target occurrences across at least 12 genuinely independent physical documents and at least 3 chronological bins.
next_gate.critical_independence_rule: Rhind EA10057, EA10058 and Brooklyn 37.1784Ea-b remain one physical-document independence group.
